diagnostic_evaluation.clinical_disclaimer: Important Medical Disclaimer: BrightPath is an educational learning and developmental engagement tool. Facial expressions, gameplay scores, and interaction latency CANNOT diagnose autism spectrum disorders or historical subtypes. Formal diagnosis requires comprehensive assessment by qualified medical and developmental specialists.
diagnostic_evaluation.historical_context_summary: Autistic Disorder, Asperger Syndrome, Childhood Disintegrative Disorder, and PDD-NOS are historical diagnostic categories from DSM-IV. In DSM-5 and ICD-11, these subtypes were unified under a single Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis.

categories.current_status: Consolidated into Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5 / ICD-11.
categories.clinical_note: Webcam expressions and game scores cannot diagnose Autistic Disorder. Clinical diagnosis requires standardized evaluation by licensed professionals.

categories.current_status: Subsumed under Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5 / ICD-11.
categories.clinical_note: Gameplay interaction metrics cannot establish Asperger traits. Formal diagnostic evaluation requires clinical history and observation.

categories.current_status: Unified under Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5; rare neurodevelopmental condition.
categories.clinical_note: This rare condition involves profound developmental regression and cannot be detected or assessed by web application interactions.

categories.category_name: Pervasive Developmental Disorder - Not Otherwise Specified (PDD-NOS)
categories.current_status: Reclassified under Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Social Communication Disorder in DSM-5.
categories.clinical_note: Subthreshold diagnostic categories are not computable from mini-game metrics. Only a qualified clinician can interpret developmental patterns.

diagnosticResults.clinical_disclaimer: Important Medical Disclaimer: BrightPath is an educational play and developmental engagement application. Facial expressions, game scores, and keyboard rhythm CANNOT diagnose autism spectrum disorders or differentiate historical diagnostic subtypes. Formal clinical diagnosis requires comprehensive assessment by qualified medical and developmental specialists.
diagnosticResults.historical_context_summary: Autistic Disorder, Asperger Syndrome, Childhood Disintegrative Disorder, and PDD-NOS are historical diagnostic categories from DSM-IV. In DSM-5 and ICD-11, these subtypes were consolidated into a single Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis.

categories.current_status: Reclassified under Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5 / ICD-11.
categories.clinical_note: Single-session educational gameplay or facial expressions cannot diagnose Autistic Disorder. Clinical diagnosis requires standardized evaluation (e.g., ADOS-2, ADI-R) by licensed practitioners.

categories.current_status: Consolidated into Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5 / ICD-11, often described dimensional as ASD without intellectual or language impairment.
categories.clinical_note: A game interface or webcam emotion detection cannot establish Asperger traits. Formal diagnostic differentiation requires developmental history and clinician observation.

categories.current_status: Subsumed into Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in DSM-5; rare neurodevelopmental condition requiring extensive pediatric neurology and developmental workup.
categories.clinical_note: This rare historical condition involves profound neurodevelopmental regression that cannot be detected or assessed by web application interactions.

categories.category_name: Pervasive Developmental Disorder - Not Otherwise Specified (PDD-NOS)
categories.current_status: Reclassified within the unified Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Social (Pragmatic) Communication Disorder in modern diagnostic manuals.
categories.clinical_note: Subthreshold diagnostic categories are not computable from client-side mini-game metrics. Only a qualified clinician can interpret developmental patterns.
